blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Equipping artificial agents with spatial intelligence requires a comprehensive generative prior over the dynamic 3D world.
We propose World Motion Models (WMMs) that capture “what was, is, and will be where across time” via sparse SE(3) pose trajectories .
WMMs are built on the observation that elements of dynamic scenes can be well approximated by a set of rigid SE(3) trajectories, a minimal yet expressive primitive for 4D modeling.
This representation unifies articulated objects, human bodies, hand-object interactions, piecewise-rigid scene dynamics, camera motion, and even robot states and actions into a single shared space. Given this representation, we cast the joint distribution of these entities as a flexible sequence modeling problem, utilizing flow-matching with per-token noise levels. Coupled with a context token mechanism for non-sequential conditioning, this formulation supports any-to-any marginal conditioning across an arbitrary number of entities and time steps. Tasks such as future prediction, motion infilling, model-predictive control, inverse kinematics, cross-embodiment retargeting, and policy learning all reduce to the application of different masks over the same network. Experiments on 6 diverse applications of 3D vision and robotics demonstrate the versatility and flexibility of WMMs with strong performance.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The world that surrounds us is inherently three-dimensional and highly dynamic—a 4D space where perception and interaction are fundamentally tied to movement. Physical actions are achieved by moving limbs or end-effectors, generating forces that translate into the motion of objects, while other agents dynamically navigate and act within this same environment. As humans, we naturally develop a strong prior over these moving entities: we intuitively anticipate how others will move, plan the physical motions required to achieve a desired goal, and foresee the physical consequences of our own actions.
To act and reason in the physical world, intelligent systems benefit from the same capability: a generative prior over the 4D world that captures the evolution of “what” and “where” across time.
blocks.zh:
环绕我们的世界本质上是三维和高度动态的——一个感知和互动与运动有根本联系的四维空间。 物理动作是通过移动四肢或末端效应器实现的,产生力量转化为物体的运动,而其他物剂则在同样的环境中动态地导航和作用. 作为人类,我们自然在这些移动的实体上发展出一个强大的前身:我们直觉地预见到其他人将如何行动,规划实现预期目标所需的物理运动,以及预见我们自己行动的实际后果.
为了在物理世界中采取行动和理性,智能系统从同样的能力中获益:一种在四维世界之前的遗传学,它捕捉“什么”和“何处”跨越时间的演变。

blocks.en: In this work, we present a unified generative model which provides a general prior over the dynamic 3D world. Our approach is highly flexible with minimal assumptions and handles unstructured scenes and arbitrary object categories. By supporting various prompting modes, a single model enables diverse inference tasks ranging from world modeling (e.g., action-conditioned/free future prediction) to complex planning (e.g., motion infilling, inverse dynamics).
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们提出了统一的基因模型,它为动态的3D世界提供了一般的前身. 我们的方法非常灵活,只有最低限度的假设,处理无结构的场景和任意的对象类别. 通过支持各种催化模式,一个单一的模型可以实现从世界建模(如行动条件/自由未来预测)到复杂规划(如运动填充,反向动态)等多种多样的推论任务.

blocks.en:
To build such a prior, we first need a unified representation that expresses the dynamic world in a physically grounded manner.
Our insight is that complex, dense motion of the physical world can be compactly approximated by a sparse set of moving coordinate frames — specifically S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) trajectories. Most entities of interest naturally reduce to this format: the dense flow of thousands of mesh vertices on a human or robot collapses into tens of joint trajectories [ 60 , 36 ] ; cameras and rigid objects track as single moving frames; and even non-rigid scene dynamics can be represented as interpolations of a small S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) motion basis [ 85 , 43 , 49 ] . We therefore adopt the S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) trajectory as our basic language for what is where across time .
These S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) trajectories subsume prior point trajectories in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} but can be far sparser, replacing, for instance, the flow of thousands of mesh vertices with the tens of joint poses of a SMPL human [ 60 ] or a robot [ 36 ] . We further impose no category-specific structure: every entity is treated equally as a pose proxy, generalizing class-bound representations (SMPL [ 60 ] , MANO [ 80 ] , URDFs) to any unstructured scene.
It is also orthogonal to video-based world modeling [ 9 , 92 , 70 , 3 , 103 ] , which captures dynamics implicitly through color changes on a screen, entangling the underlying 3D motion with appearance, lighting, and viewpoint changes. In short, the S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) trajectory provides a highly compact, physically grounded 3D abstraction for modeling arbitrary motion.
blocks.zh:
为了建立这样一个先天性,我们首先需要一种统一的代表性,以实际的方式表达充满活力的世界。
我们的洞察力是,物理世界的复杂、密集的运动可以紧凑地由一组稀少的坐标框——特别是S E(3)SE(3)轨迹——来进行。 大多数感兴趣的实体自然会降低到这种格式:人类或机器人上数千个网状顶点的密集流动会崩溃成数十个联动轨迹[60,36];相机和刚性物体轨迹作为单动帧;甚至非刚性场景动力学可以作为小S E (3) SE (3)运动基的插值[85,43,49]. 因此,我们将SE(3)SE(3)轨迹作为我们跨越时间的基本语言。
这些 S E ( 3 ) SE (3) 轨迹包含在 R 3\ mathbb{R}^{3} 中的前点轨迹, 但可以比较稀疏, 例如, 以 SMPL 人 [60] 或机器人 [36] 的数十个联姿取代了数千个网状圆顶。 我们还不强制实行任何特定类别的结构:每个实体均被平等视为一种姿势代表,将有阶级限制的表述(SMPL [60],MANO [80],URDFs)概括到任何无结构的场景.
透过屏幕上的颜色变化来捕捉动态, 用外观、照明和观点变化来包围3D运动。 简言之,SE(3)SE(3)轨迹提供了一种高度紧凑的,物理基础的3D抽象,用于模型化任意运动.

blocks.en: The question now becomes: how do we learn a generative prior over these S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) trajectories? Since motion naturally unfolds over time, this is inherently a sequence modeling problem. Traditionally, this is treated as a strictly causal task: a standard world model or dynamics model predicts future states conditioned on past history and actions. However, humans can perform non-causal inference as well, such as determining the actions required to achieve a specific goal (inverse dynamics) or planning intermediate motions between waypoints. The inference type varies widely across applications. To support these diverse inference schemes, we propose World Motion Models (WMMs), flow-matching generative models with per-token noise levels. Inspired by Diffusion Forcing [ 15 ] and discrete diffusion [ 69 , 2 ] , WMMs treat each 6D S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) pose at a given time step as an independent token, assign each its own noise level, and denoise the entire token field in a single shared forward pass.
blocks.zh: 现在的问题是:我们如何在SE(3)SE(3)轨迹之前学习基因? 由于运动自然会随着时间推移而展开,这本来就是一个序列建模问题. 传统上,这被视为一项严格意义上的因果任务:标准的世界模型或动态模型预测以过去的历史和行动为条件的未来状态. 然而,人类也可以进行非因果推论,例如确定实现某一具体目标所需的行动(反向动态),或规划路标之间的中间运动. 各种应用的推论类型差异很大. 为了支持这些多样化的推论方案,我们提出了世界运动模型(WMMs),与每声级的流配基因模型. 受扩散强化[15]和离散扩散[69,2]的启发,WMM将每个6D S E(3) SE(3)在特定时间阶下摆出一个独立标志,指定每个自己的噪声水平,并在一个共享的前进通道中将整个标志域都抹去.

blocks.en: Once trained, a WMM admits inference over arbitrary numbers of entities and time steps simply by dictating which tokens are clean (the condition) and which are noised (the prediction). Given past tokens, it acts as a future predictor p ⁡ ( s ′ | s ) p(s^{\prime}|s) ; applied to action tokens, it becomes a feed-forward policy p ⁡ ( a | s ) p(a|s) ; and when both past states and actions are provided, it acts as an action-conditioned dynamics model p ⁡ ( s ′ | s , a ) p(s^{\prime}|s,a) supporting model-predictive control. Ultimately, WMMs realize any p ⁡ ( unknown | known ) p(\text{unknown}|\text{known}) . By simply changing what is known, the exact same network transitions seamlessly between serving as a policy, an action prior, and a world model.

blocks.en: While standard trajectory modeling assumes a strictly consecutive temporal horizon, many practical tasks require reasoning beyond it. For example, planning a complex interaction often relies on an abstract goal state situated arbitrarily far in the future. Similarly, tasks like cross-embodiment retargeting require inferring correspondences between trajectories, such as those of a human and a robot. Providing a few paired demonstration frames from outside the current episode serves as an in-context template that tells the model “what is what.” To support these non-consecutive anchors, we enhance the flexibility of WMMs by introducing a set of context S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) tokens . Rather than being bound to the continuous physical timeline of the current episode, they are assigned to a decoupled context timeline with its own learnable positional embeddings. Mechanically, these context tokens are treated identically to real trajectory tokens, meaning they can seamlessly condition the model or be generated themselves.
blocks.zh: 虽然标准轨迹建模假设一个严格连续的时间范围,但许多实际任务需要超越它来推理. 例如,规划一种复杂的互动往往依赖于一个抽象的目标状态,这种状态在将来会任意存在。 同样,像交叉化重定向这样的任务需要推断出轨迹之间的对应关系,如人类和机器人的对应关系. 从本集之外提供几组对齐的演示框作为内文模板,告诉模型“什么是什么”。 为了支持这些非连续锚,我们采用了一套上下文S E(3)SE(3)令牌,提高了WMM的灵活性。 与其与当前剧集的连续物理时间线捆绑在一起,他们被分配到一个具有自身可学习位置嵌入的脱钩上下文时间线. 在机械上,这些上下文符号与真实的轨迹符号处理相同,意思是它们可以无缝地调节模型或者自己生成.

blocks.en: Together, this general S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) formulation and our flexible sequence modeling enable WMMs to demonstrate broad versatility across applications, including robot policies and model-predictive control (MPC), scene future prediction, human-object interaction generation, and multi-embodiment humanoid retargeting (Sec. ), all with SOTA performance.
blocks.zh: 这种通用的SE(3)SE(3)配制和我们灵活的序列模型使WMM能够表现出广泛的多用途性,包括机器人政策和模型预测控制(MPC),场景未来预测,人-物体交互生成,以及多表现的人造物重定向(Sec.),都具有SOTA性能.

blocks.en:
Contributions. We propose a general formulation that uses the sparse S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) trajectory as a unified representation for 4D world modeling.
To learn a flexible generative prior over this space, we introduce WMMs, flexible flow-matching models with per-token noise levels. By supporting any-to-any marginal conditioning alongside a context token mechanism, WMMs deliver strong performance across diverse 3D vision and robotics tasks.

为了在这个空间上学习一个灵活的基因, 我们引入了WMM, 灵活的流配模型 与每个音域的噪音水平。 通过支持任何边际条件以及上下文符号机制,WMM在不同的3D视觉和机器人任务中提供强大的性能.

blocks.en: 2.1 Representation: A Language for Motion Modeling
blocks.zh: 2.1 代表:一种用于模拟运动的语言

blocks.en:
World Motion Models aim to answer what was, is, and will be where across time.
The thread connecting an entity at t 1 t_{1} with the same entity at t 2 t_{2} is its motion, and motion in real-world scenes is largely low-rank: a complex scene is driven by a relatively small set of eigen rigid trajectories, while dense spatial deformation arises as a local combination of those bases [ 43 , 85 , 49 ] .
We assume the dynamic 3D world can be approximated by a finite set of rigid SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) trajectories, with dense spatial deformation recovered by interpolation, skinning, or binary assignment. SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) pose trajectories serve as the language with which we model the dynamic world. We leave modeling general linear local motion (scaling, shearing) to future work.
blocks.zh:
世界运动 模式旨在回答过去、现在和将来不同时期的问题。
连接一个实体在t 1 t_{1}和同一个实体在t 2 t_{2}的线程是它的运动,在现实世界的场景中运动基本上是低级的:一个复杂的场景是由一组相对小的eigen刚性轨迹驱动的,而密集的空间变形则作为这些基础的局部组合而产生[43,85,49].
我们假设动态的3D世界可以被一组有限的刚性SE(3)\mathrm{SE}(3)轨迹所近似,其密集的空间变形通过插值,剥皮,或二进制分配而恢复. SE QQ( 3 )\ mathrm{SE}(3) 摆出轨迹作为我们模拟动态世界的语言. 我们把模型一般线性局部运动(缩放,剪切)留给未来工作.

blocks.en: As Fig. -(A) shows, this primitive approximates the motion of the principal subjects of 3D vision and robotics. Scene future prediction over 3D point trajectories [ 47 , 46 , 36 ] is the rotation-free special case of SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) trajectories. Human and hand-object motion fits naturally: parametric body and hand models [ 60 , 80 , 106 , 48 ] are sets of bone-joint SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) frames, and articulated parts contribute additional rigid trajectories with per-part local shape. Robot kinematics treats each link as one rigid trajectory plus its mesh, the substrate for motion planning, retargeting, and control. Robot state and action are equally expressible whenever the controller (PD gains, etc.) is fixed, since the action then reduces to a set of virtual target poses. Thus, the same language captures both the observation and action of a standard control problem. Camera motion is, by definition, an SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) trajectory of the viewpoint.

blocks.en: 2.4 Implementation: Model Architecture
blocks.zh: 2.4 实施:示范结构

blocks.en:
As shown in Fig. , our model supports arbitrary numbers of entities and time steps while addressing three issues: (i) per-token noise levels : λ i , l \lambda_{i,l} has to be specified per token , not as a single global scalar as in a conventional flow-matching backbone [ 74 , 54 ] ; (ii) scale : a modest 30 30 -frame, 400 400 -trajectory scene already contains 12 12 K tokens, on which dense self-attention is expensive; (iii) missing observations : real data come with invalid intervals (occlusion, truncation, tracker drop-out) that cannot simply be masked during training. We address each as follows: (1) Per-token conditioning via AdaLN. For each token ( i , l ) (i,l) we concatenate (a) a sinusoidal embedding of λ i , l \lambda_{i,l} , (b) the feature F F , and (c) a pooled embedding of the auxiliary tokens 𝒜 \mathcal{A} (e.g. a language summary). A per-block wide multi-layer FFN maps this vector to per-token AdaLN scale-and-shift parameters that modulate every transformer block [ 74 ] . (2) Registers and factored attention. We pad the M × N M\times N token grid with three blocks of learnable registers [ 21 ] and apply five attention types on the padded grid: a self-attends across all tokens; t and p are time- and entity-axis self-attention; s and q are register-only counterparts on the same two axes, widened aggressively in channels at negligible runtime cost to add expressivity. (3) Training under missing observations. Invalid time steps must still participate in attention, since at inference the missing mask is unknown. We pin invalid tokens to λ i , l = 1 \lambda_{i,l}=1 (pure noise) and sum the loss in Eq. ( ) only over tokens with ground-truth labels.
Virtual-context tokens (Sec. ) are flagged by a 1 1 -bit prefix mask and given learnable position embeddings. Text or image tokens attach as an attention prefix.

blocks.en: WMMs can also be used as a differentiable world model rather than a plain policy. For tasks with absolute-position instructions (B2B, B2AL) in LangTable, given the generated goal state (via context tokens), we can apply model predictive control (MPC) to optimize the predicted action so as to maximize a heuristically defined value function: the similarity between the final frame of the action chunk and the generated goal. Since our model is fully differentiable, gradient-based MPC can be hybridized with sampling-based methods (full procedure in App. ); Tab. compares the plain policy with the MPC-optimized policy on B2B and B2AL, indicating both a higher success rate and faster rollout to success.

blocks.en: 3.2 TraceGen: Dense 3D Scene Future Prediction
blocks.zh: 3.2 国家 TraceGen: ense 3D 场景未来预测

blocks.en:
TraceGen [ 46 ] is a 3D trajectory generation benchmark in which the model takes a single RGB-D start frame and a language instruction and predicts the motion of 400 400 keypoints over 32 32 steps. We follow its protocol on the two subsets that provide 3D trajectories, Droid and EpicKitchen, reporting the trajectory-generation errors MSE, MAE, and endpoint MSE (each × 100 \times 100 ). Setup. Each of the 400 400 keypoints is one entity carrying a 3D position and an orientation (computed by local Procrustes in the dataset), starting at the first frame ( t = 0 t{=}0 ). We train four WMM checkpoints over the experimental space (Droid only, EpicKitchen only, and joint on both) at two keypoint window sizes ( P = 128 P{=}128 and P = 400 P{=}400 , where P P is the number of trajectories seen during training). No special context token is used in this experiment. Results. As shown in Tab. and Fig. , WMM achieves the best performance in every column in both environments.
Note that the P = 128 P=128 variant is trained with 128 128 randomly selected trajectories, meaning that it can accept random queries during inference.
Although only 128 128 trajectories are observed in parallel during training, the model can directly infer all 400 400 trajectories and even achieves better performance (P=128 wins all metrics); we hypothesize that this stems from the random sampling of 128 128 out of 400 400 trajectories during training, which prevents overfitting. The experiments also show that joint training across both domains is feasible, suggesting that future work can pursue a single unified model across domains.

blocks.en: 3.4 Human and Humanoid: Kinematic Retargeting

blocks.en:
We construct a benchmark that takes a SMPL human motion sequence and produces a Unitree G1 humanoid [ 84 ] trajectory. We evaluate retargeting quality by feeding the trajectory to a low-level robot controller (TWIST [ 97 ] ), rolling it out in physics simulation, and measuring tracking error and success rate.
Three input settings probe WMMs’ flexibility: clean human input at 30 30 FPS; sparse keyframes at 3 3 FPS that the model must infill; and human input with noise at every frame ( σ = 0.1 \sigma{=}0.1 on axis-angle and root translation). Setup. The entity set comprises the SMPL human and the G1 humanoid links, paired across embodiments inside the Context-token exemplar frames (Sec. ; two samples in Fig. ). A WMM is trained on a mix of AMASS [ 64 ] and Embody3D [ 66 ] ; a single checkpoint serves all three settings. The humanoid’s kinematic reference (ground truth) is obtained by running and filtering PHUMA [ 45 ] , a slow offline optimization method. Results. Tab. and Fig. report the comparison against GMR [ 1 ] and PHUMA [ 45 ] . GMR is a fast, real-time method but provides limited quality; PHUMA is an offline optimization method that produces more physically plausible results (less overlap, etc.) but is slow. The resulting WMM is a retargeting prior that is fast (note the throughput reported in the first column) and learns a prior over physically plausible, safe motion across sequences, providing higher-quality and safer retargeting motion. Fig. also shows real-world monocular-video-based humanoid retargeting and control results.

blocks.en: 4 Related Work
blocks.zh: 4 相关工作

blocks.en: Existing generative motion models are fragmented by actor class through morphology-specific parameterizations [ 83 , 41 , 53 ] , while general unified approaches [ 47 , 36 , 70 ] operate in dense observation spaces such as pixel-aligned point tracks, 3D flow, or video entangling 3D dynamics with appearance, or solely in 2D pixel motion space [ 77 , 68 , 78 ] . A piecewise-rigid lineage uses S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) transforms [ 10 , 33 ] but is restricted to single-agent or fixed-object settings. WMMs instead encode every moving unit (robot link, body part, scene primitive) as a (sparse) set of S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) tokens in a shared abstraction, leading to a potentially more unified and shared motion prior over all moving subjects in the physical world.
blocks.zh: 现有的基因运动模型通过形态学特定的参数化[83,41,53],按演员类别分解,而一般统一的方法[47,36,70]则在像素相通点轨迹,3D流线,或视频将3D动力学与外观结合等密集的观测空间中运行,或仅在2D像素运动空间中运行[77,68,78]. 成片固定的线条使用S E (3) SE (3)转换[10,33],但仅限于单剂或固定对象设置. WMM转而将每个移动单元(机器人链接,身体部分,场景原始)编码为SE(3)SE(3)符号的(spare)集,在一个共享抽象中,导致在物理世界中所有移动主体之前,一个潜在的更统一和共享的运动.

blocks.en:
Recent work couples world modeling with policy via video–action models [ 56 , 105 , 52 ] or latent-dynamics planners [ 29 , 28 ] , but ties the world model to a fixed morphology or pixel tokens.
Diffusion Forcing [ 15 ] and discrete masked diffusion [ 2 ] introduce per-token noise schedules for flexible conditioning.
Specifically, Diffusion Forcing [ 15 ] is the modeling method closest to ours. Although theoretically general, it primarily focuses on temporal scheduling across sequence frames. Our method generalizes the idea of per-token noise to spatial and temporal axes, and our architectural design makes this practical for more than 10K tokens.
We provide a unified representation of heterogeneous SE(3) trajectories and add a decoupled context-token mechanism, so one network spans prediction, policy rollout, and non-causal planning. See App. for an extended discussion.
blocks.zh:
最近的工作伴侣们通过视频-行动模型[56, 105, 52] 或潜在动力学规划师[29, 28] 来建立政策模型,但将世界模型与固定形态或像素符号联系起来。
扩散强化[15]和离散的遮盖扩散[2]引入了用于柔性调制的按键噪声表.
具体地说,扩散强化[15]是最接近我们的模型制作方法. 虽然理论上是笼统的,但它主要侧重于跨序列框架的时间调度. 我们的方法将每声噪声的概念概括到空间和时间轴上,我们的建筑设计使这个概念对超过10K个符号是实用的.
我们提供不同SE(3)轨迹的统一代表,并增加一个脱钩的上下文机制,因此一个网络跨越预测、政策推出和非因果关系规划。 详细讨论见App.。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We propose World Motion Models, a unified generative prior over the dynamic 3D world via sparse SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) pose trajectories. A per-token-noise-level flow-matching model with context tokens supports any-marginal conditional inference from one network, attaining state-of-the-art results on policy learning, scene future prediction, human-object interaction, and humanoid retargeting.
blocks.zh: 我们提议世界运动 模型(Models),一个在动态的3D世界之前通过稀疏的SE QQ(3)\mathrm{SE}(3) 呈现出轨迹的统一基因. 带有上下文符号的每肯-噪声级流量比对模型支持一个网络的任何边际有条件的推论,在政策学习、场景未来预测、人与对象的相互作用以及人造物重新瞄准方面实现最新结果。

blocks.en: (i) We train one WMM checkpoint per benchmark; joint training across domains and increasing the amount of supervision data are left to future work. (ii) Generalizing S ​ E ​ ( 3 ) SE(3) to more general linear groups is also a future direction. (iii) The current framework requires geometry (e.g., depth and estimated current and past states) as input; relaxing these requirements and enabling direct inference from RGB videos are also directions for future work. (iv) Another limitation of the current model is that it does not generalize to novel morphologies unseen during training; further investigation of in-context learning with our proposed context mechanism may suggest solutions in the future.
blocks.zh: (i) 我们每个基准培训一个WMM检查站;跨领域的联合培训以及增加监督数据的数量留给今后的工作。 (二)将SE(3)SE(3)概括到更一般的线性组也是未来的方向. (三)当前框架要求几何学(如深度和估计的当前状态和过去状态)作为输入;放松这些要求,使RGB视频能够直接推论,也是未来工作的方向. (四) 现行模式的另一个局限是,它没有概括到培训期间所看不到的新形态;进一步调查与我们拟议背景机制的内在学习,可能建议今后的解决办法。

blocks.en: WMM may have benefits in robotics, mixed reality, animation, games, and simulation. We do not see major direct negative ethical or societal consequences of our work.
blocks.zh: WMM可能在机器人,混杂现实,动画,游戏,和模拟等方面有益处. 我们不认为我们的工作会对道德或社会产生重大的直接负面后果。

blocks.en: Generative motion modeling has historically fragmented along actor classes. Body, human-human interaction, hand-object interaction, and scene dynamics each use their own state parameterization and task interface [ 83 , 41 , 7 , 90 , 50 , 23 ] . A more recent line of work on unification scales LM backbones, million-scale corpora, compositional priors, and motion-understanding foundations on human motion alone [ 53 , 99 , 87 , 4 , 72 , 91 , 67 ] , and three further papers consolidate human-side tasks under a single prior. MAGNet [ 65 ] models multi-agent body behavior with diffusion-forced canonical pairwise transforms, UMO [ 20 ] casts object-aware human motion as a unified in-context problem, and FUSION [ 25 ] trains an unconditional SMPL-X body and hand prior. All of these inherit a body-parametric state and so remain actor-homogeneous within the human family. A second line writes motion into a shared observation space that crosses morphologies. MoMap [ 47 ] diffuses pixel-aligned dense 3D motion maps; PointWorld [ 36 ] rolls point cloud and gripper flow as a forward simulator; TraceGen [ 46 ] flow-matches camera-frame 3D traces conditioned on a single RGB-D start frame and language; GeneralFlow [ 96 ] predicts dense 3D flow from RGB-D; EC-Flow [ 18 ] maps embodiment-centric pixel flow to end-effector SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) via inverse kinematics; ATM [ 88 ] pretrains 2D point tracks as a representation for behavior cloning; TAPNext [ 102 ] casts point tracking itself as causal next-token prediction; and sparse-track or sparse-observation diffusion also extends to dexterous manipulation and SMPL completion [ 44 , 13 ] . These methods share an observation space across actors, but the underlying tokens are translation-only points or dense flow that carry no per-entity identity and discard the rigid-body rotation that drives contact and articulation. A third line generates ambient 4D scene dynamics with explicit trajectories: Comp4D [ 89 ] factorizes a 4D world into per-object trajectories plus per-object deformation, and TC4D [ 5 ] conditions 4D generation on explicit SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) trajectories, but both target per-scene synthesis rather than a generative prior over heterogeneous moving entities. A piecewise-rigid lineage models scenes directly as per-part SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) transforms: SE3-Nets [ 10 ] and SE3-Pose-Nets [ 11 ] warp tabletop point clouds through K K learned rigid motions conditioned on one robot’s actions, OASIS [ 16 ] predicts the end-effector pose trajectory for manipulation, and SPOT [ 33 ] denoises source-target object pose trajectories from a few demonstrations, yet each remains a single-agent system over a fixed rigid-object set tied to one manipuland or one robot. The closest points of comparison to WMMs are therefore MAGNet and UMO (unified conditioning, human-only), TraceGen and MoMap (trajectory-space world modeling without rotation or per-entity identity), and SPOT together with SE3-Nets ( SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) -trajectory denoising on a fixed manipuland set), each of which stays inside one of these regimes. WMMs instead encode every moving unit, whether a robot link, hand, body, object, or scene primitive, as a sparse SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) token in a shared rot6d+translation space (Sec. ), so one denoiser is promptable across actor classes and queries arbitrary entities at arbitrary time steps, rather than tracking a fixed dense grid of points or a single morphology family.

blocks.en: A unified motion substrate must also support rollout and policy. Pixel-space world-action models keep the substrate in 2D video: DreamDojo [ 26 ] , DreamZero [ 94 ] , and Cosmos [ 70 ] synthesize frames or extract actions from pretrained video diffusion backbones, and World-VLA-Loop [ 56 ] closes the action-perception loop on this pixel substrate with a vision-language-action policy. A related dense-observation model, DyWA [ 63 ] , runs dynamics-adaptive world-action coupling over single-view point clouds for non-prehensile manipulation, swapping pixel tokens for a 3D point cloud but keeping the world model in a dense observation space. Latent-dynamics planners abstract observations into a learned latent representation: Hierarchical Humanoid WM [ 29 ] and DreamerV3 [ 28 ] couple latent rollouts with model-predictive control or value-based control, but each instance hard-codes the morphology or the target RL environment. Two recent approaches directly model heterogeneous forward dynamics: Cross-Embodiment WM [ 30 ] runs particle-graph rollouts and Geom4D-Robot [ 59 ] jointly denoises RGB and pointmap, yet both recover SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) only post-hoc through an additional pose-extraction step rather than treating SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) as the modeling primitive; imagination-policy goal generators [ 34 ] and long-horizon scene or traffic generators [ 98 , 75 ] likewise stay morphology- or domain-locked. Vision-language-action policies form a complementary set of output interfaces over various tokenizations of action [ 79 , 8 , 101 ] , and Moto [ 17 ] bridges video pretraining to action through a latent motion-token language. Most closely related to our unification approach, UWM [ 105 ] and UVA [ 52 ] jointly denoise video and action and pursue multi-axis flexibility through shared backbones, but both still tie the world-model side to pixel tokens. WMMs close this gap by predicting SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) trajectories of every tracked entity under a per-token conditioning mask, so one flow-matching model with per-token noise serves as a policy, predictor, and world simulator across arm, humanoid, dexterous hand, human, and tabletop settings, with no morphology-specific head and no separate world and policy modules (Sec. ).

blocks.en: Diffusion forcing [ 15 ] assigns each token an independent noise level, so any subset of tokens can be revealed, in-filled, or rolled out from one trained network, and CausalFusion [ 22 ] reconciles autoregressive and diffusion training under the same per-token schedule. This primitive has propagated along several tracks: streaming video adopts diffusion forcing for long-horizon rollouts and live generation [ 37 , 55 , 35 ] ; motion and robot control adopt the same schedule on body, action, or interaction tokens [ 12 , 39 , 32 , 38 ] ; discrete and masked sequence models reach the same flexible-conditioning behavior through token-level masking schedules [ 2 , 86 , 14 ] ; a separate trajectory-level denoising line conditions whole state-action plans on goals or rewards [ 40 , 19 ] ; and earlier flexible-conditioning recipes provide classifier-free guidance, masked image inpainting, and masked motion completion [ 31 , 61 , 82 ] . Each of these instances, however, binds the per-token schedule to a single domain: video frames, one actor’s skeletal tokens, one morphology’s action horizon, or text. WMMs apply the same per-token noise schedule to SE ⁡ ( 3 ) \mathrm{SE}(3) trajectories of heterogeneous entities (Sec. ) and extend the trajectory with a context token prefix on a separate timeline for non-causal anchors such as goal states or retargeting exemplars (Sec. ), so one trained network selects between motion synthesis, future prediction, policy rollout, and planning based solely on which tokens are noised at inference (Sec. ).

blocks.en: WMMs are trained on a bounded number of entities and time steps, yet many uses require more entities or time steps than fit in one forward pass (even though RoPE helps to generalize beyond the context window): long-horizon rollouts, dense scene flow, and multi-agent simulations. Splitting into independent chunks fails because two chunks denoised independently disagree at their interface. The anchored sliding-window sampler in Alg. instead exploits asynchronous-noise training to keep partially denoised tokens of one chunk as fixed anchors when denoising the next. With a context size S S and an anchor count A < S A<S , the sampler descends a discrete schedule λ K > ⋯ > λ 0 = 0 \lambda_{K}>\cdots>\lambda_{0}=0 , so that every forward pass sees S S entities at consistent asynchronous levels, exactly the regime used in training with ( ). The A A shared anchors stitch successive batches into a globally consistent rollout. Asynchronous training plus a non-grid token interface together unlock arbitrarily many entities and time steps at inference.

blocks.en: no AdaLN replaces the per-DiT-block shift/scale/gate modulation with a single zero-init linear input fusion at the token-grid input, forcing conditioning to propagate through residuals only. no per-token noise replaces the asynchronous per-token noise schedule of Sec. with a single shared diffusion timestep t t per sample, broadcast to all valid positions; at inference, known tokens are clamped via a noised q-sample with soft blending at strength 0.5 0.5 .
blocks.zh: 无 AdaLN 取代每DiT 块的移/尺度/门调制,在符格输入时使用单一的0-init线性输入聚变,迫使调制只通过残基传播. 不得用每个样本的单一共享扩散时间步 t t 来取代Sec的同步的每个音节噪音表,并广播到所有有效位置;推论,已知的音节通过无名的q-样本夹住,以0.5的强度进行软混合。

blocks.en: The reported model for TraceGen uses the ‘tpsqspt‘ layer configuration as in Fig. ; no register pool collapses the middle three layers to plain DiT at the wide dimension, removing the register-compression path and yielding the ‘tpaaapt‘ layer configuration; plain DiT collapses all seven layers to plain DiT, removing every architectural primitive and yielding the ‘aaaaaaa‘ layer configuration.
blocks.zh: TraceGen的上报模型采用了Fig中的“tpsqspt”层配置;没有寄存池将中间三层倒塌到宽维的平原DiT,去掉寄存器-压缩路径并生成“tpaaapt”层配置;Plain DiT将所有七层倒塌到平原DiT,去掉每一个建筑原始,产生“aaaaaaaaa”层配置.

blocks.en: B.5 More Details
blocks.zh: B.5 更多细节

blocks.en:
A typical WMM transformer architecture uses 8 heads with an embedding dimension of 512 and an FFN comprising a 2-layer MLP with hidden dimension 2048. The attention types are applied sequentially, one type per block. The model is trained on each application dataset using AdamW, a learning rate of 5e-5, a weight decay factor of 1e-3, and a decay step at 300K.
For each setting, we train one set of weights on a single A6000 48GB GPU using the largest batch size that fits in memory: Language Table 64; TraceGen 4/12 for P=400/128; OMOMO 16; humanoid 8.
blocks.zh:
一个典型的WMM变压器架构采用8个头,嵌入维度为512,一个FFN由2层的MLP组成,隐藏维度为2048. 注意类型依次应用,每块一个类型. 该模型使用亚当W对每个应用数据集进行训练,学习速度为5e-5,体重衰减因子为1e-3,衰减步骤为300K.
使用最大批量尺寸的内存: 语言表64; TraceGen 4/12,P=400/128;OMOMO 16;人文类8.
